analysisSteps.title: Analysis 1: Total Closed Won Revenue by Geography
analysisSteps.question: What is the total closed-won revenue achieved in the current quarter for each geographic region and segment?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data containing closed-won opportunities for the current quarter, group by [Booking Target Geo (by BT RegSeg)] and calculate the sum of [Opportunity ACV] for each geography. Present the results sorted by revenue in descending order. Identify which geographies are the top revenue contributors and which are underperforming. Provide specific revenue figures for each geography.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 2: Revenue Distribution Concentration
analysisSteps.question: What percentage of total quarterly revenue does each geography contribute, and is revenue concentration a risk?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, calculate the total sum of [Opportunity ACV] across all geographies, then for each [Booking Target Geo (by BT RegSeg)], calculate the percentage contribution to total revenue. Identify if revenue is overly concentrated in one or two geographies (e.g., top 2 geographies representing >70% of revenue), which could indicate geographic diversification risk.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 3: Revenue by Opportunity Type
analysisSteps.question: What is the revenue split between new customer acquisition and existing customer expansion in the current quarter?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [Opportunity Type] and calculate the sum of [Opportunity ACV] for each type. Calculate the percentage split between 'new customer' and 'existing customer expansion' revenue. Assess whether the balance aligns with healthy growth patterns (typically 60-70% new, 30-40% expansion) and identify if the business is overly dependent on one type.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 4: Deal Count by Owner Team
analysisSteps.question: How many closed-won deals did each owner team close in the current quarter?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [BT Region Segment (split) by Owner team (FY'26)] and count the number of opportunities (deals) for each team. Identify which teams are most productive in terms of deal volume and which teams may need support or have capacity issues.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 5: Average Deal Size by Owner Team

analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [BT Region Segment (split) by Owner team (FY'26)] and calculate the average [Opportunity ACV] for each team. Identify teams with significantly higher or lower average deal sizes, which may indicate different market segments, sales strategies, or pricing effectiveness.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 6: Total MQL Volume for Current Quarter

analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, calculate the total sum of [Person Mqls Count] for the current quarter. This represents the total MQL volume generated by marketing activities. Provide the absolute number and assess whether this volume is sufficient to support pipeline coverage requirements for future quarters.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 7: Quarter-over-Quarter MQL Trend

Calculate the quarter-over-quarter percentage change for each period. Identify whether MQL generation is growing, flat, or declining. Flag any quarters with significant drops (>20%) or spikes that require investigation.

This metric indicates the effectiveness of product-led growth initiatives and self-service acquisition channels.

Calculate the quarter-over-quarter percentage change. Assess whether free trial acquisition is growing consistently, which would indicate successful product-led growth strategies and effective web conversion.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 24: M1 Opportunity Count for New Customer
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: How many M1 stage opportunities were created for new customers in the current quarter?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] for new customer opportunities. This baseline number will be used to calculate conversion rates to subsequent stages. Note this value for comparison with S0 counts.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 25: M1-to-S0 Conversion Rate for New Customer
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity S0 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the M1-to-S0 conversion rate for new customer opportunities, and is there a qualification bottleneck?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched S0 data and the M1 count from Analysis 24, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity S0 Created Count] for new customers. Then calculate the conversion rate as (S0 Count / M1 Count) × 100. Benchmark this against typical conversion rates (usually 40-60%). If the rate is below 40%, there may be lead quality issues or qualification process bottlenecks that need addressing.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 26: S0-to-S1 Conversion Rate for New Customer
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity S1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the S0-to-S1 conversion rate for new customer opportunities, and are there issues in early qualification?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched S1 data and the S0 count from previous analysis, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity S1 Created Count] for new customers. Then calculate the conversion rate as (S1 Count / S0 Count) × 100. Benchmark this against typical rates (usually 60-75%). Low conversion rates may indicate issues with discovery processes, lack of budget qualification, or misalignment with customer needs.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 27: S1-to-S3 Conversion Rate for New Customer
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity S3 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the S1-to-S3 conversion rate for new customer opportunities, and are there bottlenecks in mid-stage progression?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched S3 data and the S1 count from previous analysis, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity S3 Created Count] for new customers. Then calculate the conversion rate as (S3 Count / S1 Count) × 100. Benchmark this against typical rates (usually 50-65%). Low conversion rates may indicate issues with technical validation, competitive losses, or pricing concerns that cause opportunities to stall.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 28: M1 Opportunity Count for Existing Customer Expansion
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: How many M1 stage opportunities were created for existing customer expansion in the current quarter?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] for existing customer expansion opportunities. This baseline will be used to assess expansion pipeline health and conversion rates, which typically differ from new customer acquisition.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 29: M1-to-S0 Conversion Rate for Existing Customer Expansion
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity S0 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the M1-to-S0 conversion rate for existing customer expansion, and how does it compare to new customer rates?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched S0 data and the M1 count from Analysis 28, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity S0 Created Count] for expansion opportunities. Calculate the conversion rate as (S0 Count / M1 Count) × 100. Compare this to the new customer conversion rate from Analysis 25. Expansion opportunities typically have higher conversion rates (60-80%) since the customer relationship exists. Lower rates may indicate customer success or account management issues.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 30: S1 Opportunity Count for Existing Customer Expansion
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity S1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: How many S1 stage opportunities exist for existing customer expansion in the current quarter?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity S1 Created Count] for existing customer expansion. This represents the mid-stage expansion pipeline and will be used to calculate conversion to late-stage opportunities.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 31: S1-to-S3 Conversion Rate for Existing Customer Expansion

analysisSteps.question: What is the S1-to-S3 conversion rate for existing customer expansion, and does it indicate healthy expansion motion?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched S3 data and the S1 count from Analysis 30, calculate the sum of [f Opportunity S3 Created Count] for expansion opportunities. Calculate the conversion rate as (S3 Count / S1 Count) × 100. Expansion opportunities typically have higher conversion rates (65-80%) than new customer deals. Lower rates may indicate pricing resistance, lack of demonstrated value, or competitive threats in the installed base.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 32: Quarter-over-Quarter Revenue Trend

Identify growth acceleration or deceleration, seasonal patterns, and assess whether the business is on track to meet annual targets. Flag any quarters with significant deviations (>15% variance) from the trend.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 35: Next Quarter Pipeline Coverage by Geography
analysisSteps.question: Does each geography have adequate S3 pipeline coverage for next quarter targets, and where are the coverage gaps?

Compare to Q+2 targets for each geography. Identify geographies with insufficient coverage (less than 5x target) that require strategic pipeline generation initiatives such as increased marketing campaigns, partner programs, or territory expansion to ensure future quarter success.
